quests.conceptTitle: Modal Meter: Urgency Levels: had better vs should
quests.question: You ___ better call the vet right now - she hasn't eaten in two days.
quests.targetSentence: You had better call the vet right now - she hasn't eaten in two days.
quests.grammarRule: Urgency Levels: had better vs should
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Had better' fits the immediate urgency created by a specific, worrying symptom, stronger than general advice.
quests.nativeTip: There's real urgency here, with a specific worrying symptom.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎚️ Modal 'had' (Modal Function (50%)) ➔ 'You had better call the vet right now - she hasn't eaten in two days.'

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Meter: Urgency Levels: had better vs should
quests.question: You ___ eat more vegetables in general - it's just healthier long-term.
quests.targetSentence: You should eat more vegetables in general - it's just healthier long-term.
quests.grammarRule: Urgency Levels: had better vs should
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Should' fits general, ongoing advice without any specific urgent trigger, unlike 'had better'.
quests.nativeTip: This is broad, ongoing lifestyle advice with no immediate crisis.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎚️ Modal 'should' (Advice / Expectation (75%)) ➔ 'You should eat more vegetables in general - it's just healthier long-term.'

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Meter: Urgency Levels: had better vs should
quests.question: We ___ better finish setting up before the guests start arriving in ten minutes.
quests.targetSentence: We had better finish setting up before the guests start arriving in ten minutes.
quests.grammarRule: Urgency Levels: had better vs should
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Had better' fits the specific, tight time pressure of guests arriving imminently.
quests.nativeTip: A specific, close deadline creates real time pressure.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎚️ Modal 'had' (Modal Function (50%)) ➔ 'We had better finish setting up before the guests start arriving in ten minutes.'

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Meter: Habitual Nuance: could vs would
quests.question: In the old factory, workers ___ operate three different machines each, depending on the shift.
quests.targetSentence: In the old factory, workers could operate three different machines each, depending on the shift.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Could' describes a general past capability workers had, distinct from 'would', which suits a repeated routine rather than a skill.
quests.nativeTip: This describes a general skill or capability workers had, not a repeated ritual.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎚️ Modal 'could' (Possibility (25%)) ➔ 'In the old factory, workers could operate three different machines each, depending on the shift.'

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Meter: Habitual Nuance: could vs would
quests.question: Every evening without fail, the old factory whistle ___ sound at exactly six o'clock.
quests.targetSentence: Every evening without fail, the old factory whistle would sound at exactly six o'clock.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Would' fits a fixed, repeated past routine, describing something that reliably happened the same way each time.
quests.nativeTip: This describes a fixed, repeated event, happening the same way every time.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎚️ Modal 'would' (Ability / Willingness (50%)) ➔ 'Every evening without fail, the old factory whistle would sound at exactly six o'clock.'

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Meter: Habitual Nuance: could vs would
quests.question: Back then, a skilled typist ___ produce over a hundred words a minute.
quests.targetSentence: Back then, a skilled typist could produce over a hundred words a minute.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Could' describes a general past capability associated with skill, distinct from a repeated daily habit.
quests.nativeTip: This is describing a general capability some people had, not a daily ritual.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎚️ Modal 'could' (Possibility (25%)) ➔ 'Back then, a skilled typist could produce over a hundred words a minute.'

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Meter: Regret vs Missed Opportunity
quests.question: You ___ have told me about the change of plans - I found out from someone else entirely.
quests.targetSentence: You should have told me about the change of plans - I found out from someone else entirely.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Should have' expresses disappointment about an unmet expectation, since telling the speaker was the considerate thing to do.
quests.nativeTip: This expresses disappointment that an expected courtesy wasn't followed.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎚️ Modal 'should' (Advice / Expectation (75%)) ➔ 'You should have told me about the change of plans - I found out from someone else entirely.'

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Meter: Regret vs Missed Opportunity
quests.question: With your connections, you ___ have introduced them to the right people months ago.
quests.targetSentence: With your connections, you could have introduced them to the right people months ago.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Could have' points out a genuine unrealized opportunity, based on the resources the person had, without framing it as a broken obligation.
quests.nativeTip: This points out an option that existed, without necessarily criticising a failed duty.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎚️ Modal 'could' (Possibility (25%)) ➔ 'With your connections, you could have introduced them to the right people months ago.'

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Meter: Regret vs Missed Opportunity
quests.question: Honestly, you ___ have warned us about the noise before we booked that room.
quests.targetSentence: Honestly, you should have warned us about the noise before we booked that room.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Should have' expresses direct criticism about an expected courtesy, framing the warning as something the listener owed them.
quests.nativeTip: This is a fairly direct criticism about something the speaker feels was owed to them.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎚️ Modal 'should' (Advice / Expectation (75%)) ➔ 'Honestly, you should have warned us about the noise before we booked that room.'

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Meter: Deduction Confidence: must have vs might have
quests.question: The exact same typo appears in both documents, so one ___ have been copied from the other.
quests.targetSentence: The exact same typo appears in both documents, so one must have been copied from the other.
quests.grammarRule: Deduction Confidence: must have vs might have
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Must have' expresses strong confidence, since an identical unusual typo is powerful evidence of copying.
quests.nativeTip: An identical, unusual detail across two documents supports strong confidence.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎚️ Modal 'must' (Obligation / Certainty (100%)) ➔ 'The exact same typo appears in both documents, so one must have been copied from the other.'

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Meter: Deduction Confidence: must have vs might have
quests.question: There's a slight resemblance in the wording, but the report ___ have been written independently.
quests.targetSentence: There's a slight resemblance in the wording, but the report might have been written independently.
quests.grammarRule: Deduction Confidence: must have vs might have
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Might have' fits a weak, vague similarity, which alone isn't strong enough evidence for a confident conclusion.
quests.nativeTip: A weak, vague similarity supports only a tentative possibility.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎚️ Modal 'might' (Possibility (25%)) ➔ 'There's a slight resemblance in the wording, but the report might have been written independently.'

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Meter: Deduction Confidence: must have vs might have
quests.question: Both witnesses independently described the same rare detail, so it ___ have actually happened that way.
quests.targetSentence: Both witnesses independently described the same rare detail, so it must have actually happened that way.
quests.grammarRule: Deduction Confidence: must have vs might have
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Must have' expresses strong confidence, since two independent witnesses agreeing on a rare detail is compelling evidence.
quests.nativeTip: Two independent, matching, unusual accounts support strong confidence.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎚️ Modal 'must' (Obligation / Certainty (100%)) ➔ 'Both witnesses independently described the same rare detail, so it must have actually happened that way.'

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Meter: Subtlety Continued: shall vs should
quests.question: ___ we say seven o'clock for the call, or does that clash with your evening?
quests.targetSentence: Shall we say seven o'clock for the call, or does that clash with your evening?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Shall we...?' naturally proposes a joint plan for agreement, distinct from 'should', which asks about advisability rather than proposing an action together.
quests.nativeTip: This is proposing a specific plan for both people to agree on.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎚️ Modal 'Shall' (Obligation / Certainty (100%)) ➔ 'Shall we say seven o'clock for the call, or does that clash with your evening?'

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Meter: Subtlety Continued: shall vs should
quests.question: Given everything that's happened, you ___ probably take a few days off to recover.
quests.targetSentence: Given everything that's happened, you should probably take a few days off to recover.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Should' offers personal, caring advice directed at an individual, a role 'shall' doesn't typically fill in modern English.
quests.nativeTip: This is personal, caring advice directed at one person.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎚️ Modal 'should' (Advice / Expectation (75%)) ➔ 'Given everything that's happened, you should probably take a few days off to recover.'

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Meter: Subtlety Continued: shall vs should
quests.question: ___ I fetch you a glass of water while you wait?
quests.targetSentence: Shall I fetch you a glass of water while you wait?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Shall I...?' naturally offers to do something helpful for someone, a distinct function from the advice-giving 'should'.
quests.nativeTip: The speaker is politely offering to do something for someone else.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎚️ Modal 'Shall' (Obligation / Certainty (100%)) ➔ 'Shall I fetch you a glass of water while you wait?'

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Meter: Register Nuance: can vs could requests
quests.question: ___ you just quickly check that number for me? Two seconds, tops.
quests.targetSentence: Can you just quickly check that number for me? Two seconds, tops.
quests.grammarRule: Register Nuance: can vs could requests
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Can' fits this light, breezy request, reinforced by casual softeners like 'just' and 'quickly'.
quests.nativeTip: This is a quick, breezy request, softened by 'just' and 'quickly'.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎚️ Modal 'Can' (Ability / Willingness (50%)) ➔ 'Can you just quickly check that number for me? Two seconds, tops.'

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Meter: Register Nuance: can vs could requests
quests.question: I hate to ask, but ___ you possibly cover my shift this Saturday?
quests.targetSentence: I hate to ask, but could you possibly cover my shift this Saturday?
quests.grammarRule: Register Nuance: can vs could requests
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Could' fits a more carefully hedged request, appropriate when asking for a bigger favour that requires extra politeness.
quests.nativeTip: This request is hedged carefully, suggesting a bigger favour is being asked.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎚️ Modal 'could' (Possibility (25%)) ➔ 'I hate to ask, but could you possibly cover my shift this Saturday?'

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Meter: Register Nuance: can vs could requests
quests.question: ___ I grab a napkin from over there real quick?
quests.targetSentence: Can I grab a napkin from over there real quick?
quests.grammarRule: Register Nuance: can vs could requests
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Can' fits the small, casual nature of this request in a relaxed, informal setting.
quests.nativeTip: This is a very small, casual request in an informal setting.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎚️ Modal 'Can' (Ability / Willingness (50%)) ➔ 'Can I grab a napkin from over there real quick?'

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Meter: Permission/Possibility Mixed
quests.question: Under exceptional circumstances, the panel ___ waive the usual application fee entirely.
quests.targetSentence: Under exceptional circumstances, the panel may waive the usual application fee entirely.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'May' fits the formal, policy tone describing a discretionary power the panel holds under specific conditions.
quests.nativeTip: This describes a formal discretionary power, stated in a policy tone.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎚️ Modal 'may' (Possibility (25%)) ➔ 'Under exceptional circumstances, the panel may waive the usual application fee entirely.'

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Meter: Permission/Possibility Mixed
quests.question: It's hard to say for sure, but the numbers ___ improve slightly next quarter.
quests.targetSentence: It's hard to say for sure, but the numbers might improve slightly next quarter.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Might' fits a genuinely uncertain guess, appropriate for the casual hedge 'it's hard to say for sure'.
quests.nativeTip: This is a genuinely uncertain, informal-sounding guess.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎚️ Modal 'might' (Possibility (25%)) ➔ 'It's hard to say for sure, but the numbers might improve slightly next quarter.'

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Meter: Permission/Possibility Mixed
quests.question: Staff ___ request an extension of up to five working days, subject to manager approval.
quests.targetSentence: Staff may request an extension of up to five working days, subject to manager approval.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'May' fits a formal entitlement described in policy language, tied to an explicit condition (manager approval).
quests.nativeTip: This is a formal, policy-based entitlement subject to a condition.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎚️ Modal 'may' (Possibility (25%)) ➔ 'Staff may request an extension of up to five working days, subject to manager approval.'

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Meter: Prediction/Hypothetical Mixed
quests.question: If the current growth rate holds steady, revenue ___ double within three years.
quests.targetSentence: If the current growth rate holds steady, revenue would double within three years.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Would' fits the result of a hypothetical condition, describing an imagined future scenario rather than a settled prediction.
quests.nativeTip: This is the result clause of a hypothetical condition about the future.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎚️ Modal 'would' (Ability / Willingness (50%)) ➔ 'If the current growth rate holds steady, revenue would double within three years.'

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Meter: Prediction/Hypothetical Mixed
quests.question: Barring any last-minute issues, the launch ___ go ahead exactly as scheduled.
quests.targetSentence: Barring any last-minute issues, the launch will go ahead exactly as scheduled.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Will' fits a confident, near-certain prediction about a scheduled event, given the condition is stated as unlikely to occur.
quests.nativeTip: This is a confident, near-certain prediction about a planned event.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎚️ Modal 'will' (Obligation / Certainty (100%)) ➔ 'Barring any last-minute issues, the launch will go ahead exactly as scheduled.'

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Meter: Prediction/Hypothetical Mixed
quests.question: If we'd invested earlier, the returns ___ have been far greater by now.
quests.targetSentence: If we'd invested earlier, the returns would have been far greater by now.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Would have' completes the third conditional, describing the imagined result of a past decision that wasn't made.
quests.nativeTip: This is the imagined result of an unreal past condition.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎚️ Modal 'would' (Ability / Willingness (50%)) ➔ 'If we'd invested earlier, the returns would have been far greater by now.'

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Meter: Obligation Source: must vs have to
quests.question: I ___ finish this report tonight - my manager set a strict deadline for tomorrow morning.
quests.targetSentence: I have to finish this report tonight - my manager set a strict deadline for tomorrow morning.
quests.grammarRule: Obligation Source: must vs have to
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Have to' expresses an obligation imposed by an external authority (the manager's deadline), distinct from 'must', which often signals the speaker's own sense of necessity.
quests.nativeTip: The obligation comes from an outside authority, not the speaker's own feeling.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎚️ Modal 'have to' (Obligation / Certainty (100%)) ➔ 'I have to finish this report tonight - my manager set a strict deadline for tomorrow morning.'

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Meter: Obligation Source: must vs have to
quests.question: I ___ apologise to her myself - it's simply the right thing for me to do.
quests.targetSentence: I must apologise to her myself - it's simply the right thing for me to do.
quests.grammarRule: Obligation Source: must vs have to
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Must' here reflects the speaker's own internal sense of obligation, rather than a rule imposed from outside.
quests.nativeTip: This obligation comes from the speaker's own personal sense of what's right.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎚️ Modal 'must' (Obligation / Certainty (100%)) ➔ 'I must apologise to her myself - it's simply the right thing for me to do.'

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Meter: Obligation Source: must vs have to
quests.question: Under the visa conditions, applicants ___ provide biometric data at the embassy.
quests.targetSentence: Under the visa conditions, applicants have to provide biometric data at the embassy.
quests.grammarRule: Obligation Source: must vs have to
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Have to' fits an obligation clearly imposed by an external authority - the visa conditions - rather than personal judgement.
quests.nativeTip: This obligation is imposed by an official external requirement.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎚️ Modal 'have to' (Obligation / Certainty (100%)) ➔ 'Under the visa conditions, applicants have to provide biometric data at the embassy.'

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Meter: Integrated High-Level Distinctions
quests.question: Given that both independent audits reached the same conclusion, the figures ___ be accurate.
quests.targetSentence: Given that both independent audits reached the same conclusion, the figures must be accurate.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Must' fits the strong confidence justified by two separate, independent audits reaching the same conclusion.
quests.nativeTip: Two independent confirmations justify high confidence.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎚️ Modal 'must' (Obligation / Certainty (100%)) ➔ 'Given that both independent audits reached the same conclusion, the figures must be accurate.'

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Meter: Integrated High-Level Distinctions
quests.question: You ___ really have double-checked those figures before sending them to the board.
quests.targetSentence: You should really have double-checked those figures before sending them to the board.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Should have' expresses hindsight criticism about a preventable oversight, distinct from 'could have', which would only note an available option.
quests.nativeTip: This is hindsight criticism of a preventable oversight.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎚️ Modal 'should' (Advice / Expectation (75%)) ➔ 'You should really have double-checked those figures before sending them to the board.'

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Meter: Integrated High-Level Distinctions
quests.question: ___ it be possible to see the revised figures before Thursday's meeting?
quests.targetSentence: Could it be possible to see the revised figures before Thursday's meeting?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Could it be possible...?' offers a carefully polite, indirect way of making a professional request.
quests.nativeTip: This is a careful, professional, indirect request.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎚️ Modal 'Could' (Possibility (25%)) ➔ 'Could it be possible to see the revised figures before Thursday's meeting?'
